Both teams enter 8-2 playing for an early NFC tiebreaker edge — elevated stakes for both sides cut against either team being flat (SI.com NFC North coverage) — neutral context.

games.thirdReasoning: Dallas' offense (51 points, 480 yards last week) against the NFL's worst takeaway defense, plus Philadelphia starting its third different QB of the season on the road, points to a comfortable Dallas cover of 8.5. The most surprising angle is that Milton was a Cowboys castoff himself. Dallas' shaky 3-5 ATS record as a favorite and Eagles' banged-up corners are the main things that could keep it inside the number, but neither offsets the offense/defense mismatch. Would flip toward an Eagles backdoor cover only if Dallas empties the bench with a big fourth-quarter lead.
thirdResearch: [angle] Eagles QB Jalen Hurts is out for the season after blood clots were found in his lungs in October; backup Tanner McKee started 3 games before being benched, and Joe Milton — whom Dallas itself waived after the preseason — is Philadelphia's QB making a homecoming start against his old team (multiple outlets, Oct-Nov 2026) — helps Cowboys.

[angle] Milton was on the Cowboys' own practice squad before Philadelphia signed him off it; Dallas-market media are framing this as Milton getting a shot to 'ruin the holidays' at AT&T Stadium if he upsets his former team (AtoZ Sports, Nov 2026) — real narrative fuel, could cut either way.

[angle] Philadelphia is the NFL's worst takeaway defense at 0.5 per game (32nd of 32), while Dallas is coming off 480 total yards and 51 points on Tennessee — the Cowboys don't need to force mistakes to move the ball (TeamRankings, CBS box score) — helps Cowboys.

Eagles starting CB Jonathan Jones did not practice Wednesday (ankle), and CB1 Quinyon Mitchell only just returned from missing Week 11 himself — Philadelphia's secondary is banged up against CeeDee Lamb (CBS Sports injury report) — helps Cowboys.

Cowboys starting guard Tyler Booker has not practiced and TE Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle) is in danger of missing another game, a dent in Dallas' interior protection and red-zone targeting (CBS Sports injury report) — helps Eagles.

The spread has barely moved since the early-offseason look-ahead line (Cowboys -8.5 then and now), unusual given Dallas' 5-6 record — a sign the market is pricing Philadelphia's QB situation, not the records (Covers.com, FOX Sports) — helps Cowboys (spread-specific).

Dallas is only 3-5 ATS as a favorite this season, failing to cover in losses to the Giants, Buccaneers, Packers, Cardinals and Colts — a real chance the Cowboys win big but still don't clear 8.5 (StatMuse) — helps Eagles (spread-specific).

Philadelphia is 0-3 ATS as a favorite in the games StatMuse tracks and has no recorded underdog cover yet, but Dak Prescott has multiple-interception games this season (Oct. 8 vs. Tampa Bay, Oct. 18 at Green Bay) that can open the door to a backdoor cover late (StatMuse) — helps Eagles (spread-specific, modest hedge).

Philadelphia's offense ranks dead last in the league in yards per play (4.3), the widest gap of any game on the Thanksgiving slate — exactly the kind of mismatch that has produced Dallas blowouts this season (season team stats) — helps Cowboys outright, modest Eagles backdoor-cover hedge.

Dallas is playing its first Thanksgiving home game since the 2025 death of DL Marshawn Kneeland, an emotional/legacy thread players have referenced pregame this season (6abc, 2026 reporting) — context only.

[angle] This FOX Thanksgiving window was built around the Eagles-Cowboys rivalry, and Dallas players have talked about wanting to be the team that finally 'breaks the Thanksgiving curse' against Philadelphia (SI.com) — mild extra motivation for Dallas at home.

games.thirdReasoning: Weather, Kansas City's O-line injuries, and Buffalo's rivalry dominance are real, but they're already baked into a short home-favorite number. Kansas City's top-5 scoring defense and the model's own blowout-regression flag on Buffalo's win over Miami (driven by Josh Allen's turnover risk and a bought-in market number) suggest the Chiefs keep this inside a field goal. The most surprising angle is that Buffalo, the rivalry's recent owner, is also this week's statistically flagged regression candidate. Would flip to Buffalo if the rain is heavier than modeled or if Kansas City's O-line injuries prove costlier than the number reflects.
thirdResearch: [angle] Buffalo has won five straight meetings in this rivalry, including a 28-21 win last season, and tonight is the Bills' first-ever Thanksgiving home game — a milestone and a streak Buffalo is motivated to extend (NFL.com, SI.com) — helps Bills.

[angle] The Highmark Stadium forecast calls for the mid-30s and an 88% chance of heavy rain at kickoff — genuinely difficult passing conditions, and the kind of game Buffalo's identity is built around versus a Chiefs team more associated with dome/warm-weather comfort (weather data) — helps Bills.

[angle] Chiefs starting RT Jaylon Moore is out with a high-ankle sprain described as an injury that 'takes linemen longer to recover from,' and Kansas City's line is already uncertain after the recent promotion of depth piece Fred Johnson — a real pass-protection problem (Yardbarker Chiefs injury report) — helps Bills.
Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III is out (groin), with rookie Emmett Johnson set to be the lead back and practice-squad elevations expected — a thinned-out skill group (Yardbarker) — helps Bills.

Buffalo's own injury sheet is comparatively clean: no player was ruled out on the final report, and starters such as G O'Cyrus Torrence (hadn't missed a game since 2023) and CB Christian Benford were only limited, suggesting they're expected to play (CBS Sports) — helps Bills.

Josh Allen threw 2 interceptions in last week's win over Miami and has 9 on the season; per the model's own blowout-regression check, Buffalo's win over Miami drew 3 of 5 regression flags (market bought in, a top-5 Chiefs scoring defense, and Allen's turnover history) — helps Chiefs (spread-specific/regression hedge).

Kansas City's defense ranks 2nd in the NFL in points allowed (16.3/game) and 7th in pass defense, giving the Chiefs a credible path to keeping this inside a field goal even if the offense is playing from a slim deficit (TeamRankings) — helps Chiefs (spread-specific).

Kansas City is only getting 3 points as a true road underdog in a game where its own per-play offense (6.3 Yds/play) narrowly outgrades Buffalo's (6.0) — a tighter number than the recent rivalry history alone would suggest (odds data, TeamRankings) — helps Chiefs (spread-specific).
Both teams enter a combined 17-3 and are playing for first place in the AFC — the highest-stakes game of the Thanksgiving slate, cutting against either team playing flat (SI.com) — neutral context.

[angle] Buffalo grades top-10 on a per-play basis on both sides of the ball (6.0 Yds/play, 20.8 points allowed/game), while Kansas City's defense leans more on limiting points than forcing turnovers (2nd in points allowed, only 15th in takeaways) — a style matchup where Buffalo doesn't need to force mistakes to control the game (TeamRankings) — helps Bills.

Both the moneyline (Bills -149/Chiefs +126) and the spread have held basically steady since the early-offseason look (Bills -2.5 then, -3 now) — no late sharp move either direction despite the public narrative around Buffalo's rivalry dominance (Covers.com/FOX Sports odds) — neutral context, mild hedge against overconfidence in Buffalo.
